name: Sacyr, S.A.
executive_summary:
Sacyr is a Spanish infrastructure group pivoting from cyclical EPC towards long-duration concessions, where recurring cash flows are the stated strategic anchor. The quantitative screen flags a buy on cash generation, dividend, GARP and risk families — notably an 18.2% FCF yield and a 4.3% dividend yield — but headline valuation (P/E 39.2, P/B 3.8) and extreme balance-sheet leverage sit awkwardly with classic deep-value criteria. Reported net profit to parent shareholders fell in FY2025 (Yahoo fallback), while operating and free cash flow strengthened materially; the central debate is whether concession cash economics justify the equity story despite thin accounting earnings and heavy debt. Primary regulatory filing bodies are absent from the research pack, so this memo relies on Yahoo financials and news headlines — a material verification gap before sizing a position.

---
investment_thesis:
For a value-oriented investor, the case rests on **cash, not reported earnings**. Sacyr passes seven of 22 screen models across all four signal families (cheapness, dividend, GARP, risk), with high data completeness (20/20 metrics). The standout inputs are FCF yield (~18%), Lynch/Neff PEG metrics (screen PEG 0.04, though distorted by a low earnings base), dividend growth, Magic Formula and Acquirer’s Multiple passes, plus Earnings Quality. Operating cash flow rose to €1.36bn in FY2025 (Yahoo) from €1.29bn in FY2024, and FCF reached €1.10bn from €961m — consistent with management’s stated “concession-first” model in which asset rotations and working-capital release fund dividends and deleveraging.

Business quality, as inferred from news flow rather than filings, appears directionally sound: recurring concession revenues, selective divestments (e.g. Columbia), and a large pipeline including Italy’s Strait of Messina bridge (Webuild–Sacyr–IHI consortium, August 2025). ROE of 11.9% is acceptable but below quality thresholds (Buffett/Moat models failed). The screen’s buy signal is **not** a Graham deep-value call — Graham, Schloss, Deep Value, Quality Value and Financial Health all failed, primarily on P/E ≥15, P/B ≥3, thin margins and **debt/equity ~417%**. The value hook is therefore a **cash-flow compounder at a transitional inflection**, not a net-net or low-multiple contrarian pick. Conviction from the screen itself is modest (30%, new signal, one week).

---
financial_review:
**Source limitation:** `filings_index.json` contains one CNMV-linked “other relevant information” entry (April 2025) with **no downloadable body**; there are **no annual or interim filing extracts** under `filings/bodies/`. All figures below are from **`financials_annual.json` (Yahoo Finance)** unless noted. Interim detail is limited to cached quarterly income in the same file; no half-year regulatory filing body is available.

### Income and cash trends (FY2022–FY2025, Yahoo)

| Metric | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 |
|--------|------|------|------|------|
| Revenue (€m) | 4,977 | 4,609 | 4,571 | 4,660 |
| EBITDA (€m) | 1,211 | 1,432 | 1,342 | 1,302 |
| Operating income (€m) | 1,224 | 1,148 | 1,185 | 1,141 |
| Net income to common (€m) | 111 | 153* | 113 | 86 |
| Diluted EPS (€) | 0.17 | 0.22 | 0.15 | 0.11 |
| Operating cash flow (€m) | 705 | 848 | 1,294 | 1,359 |
| Free cash flow (€m) | 121 | 624 | 961 | 1,104 |

*2023 net income includes €311m from discontinued operations; continuing operations net income to common was negative on a normalised basis.

**Trend commentary:** Revenue has been broadly flat since 2022 (~€4.6–5.0bn), while EBITDA peaked in 2023 and eased slightly in 2025. Reported net income attributable to shareholders **declined 24%** in 2025 (€86m vs €113m in 2024), driven in part by unusual/special charges (Yahoo shows €93m unusual items in 2025). By contrast, **operating and free cash flow improved steadily**, with FY2025 FCF exceeding FY2025 EBITDA (€1.10bn vs €1.30bn) — a pattern echoed in news (“Sacyr FY-2025: flujo de caja supera el EBITDA, deuda alcanza un mínimo histórico”, 27 February 2026). Interest expense remains heavy: €708m in 2025 (vs €749m in 2024).

### Balance sheet and leverage (Yahoo, year-end)

- **Net debt:** €7.20bn (2025) vs €8.49bn (2024) — ~€1.3bn reduction.
- **Total debt:** €9.35bn (2025) vs €10.34bn (2024).
- **Stockholders’ equity:** €1.04bn (2025); tangible book €955m.
- **Current ratio:** 1.15 (screen input) — below Graham’s 2.0 threshold.
- **Minority interests:** €1.16bn — significant non-controlling stakes in concession SPVs.

The screen’s debt/equity of ~417% and failed Financial Health model (high net debt/EBITDA, weak interest coverage) reflect a **highly levered concession structure** typical of the sector but uncomfortable for conservative value investors. Piotroski F-Score is 6/9 (failed), with ROA, current ratio and gross margin trends not improving.

### Interim / quarterly (Yahoo cache only)

Q1 2026 (quarter ending in Yahoo “2026” bucket): revenue €1.12bn; net income to common €37.5m; operating income €221m. This is a single quarter snapshot — **no H1 2026 filing body** is in the index. News on 30 July 2026 reports H1 2026 revenue and EBITDA up ~9%, record shareholder returns, Columbia divestment benefit, but **net debt rising on concession investments** — a tension not reconcilable to primary filings in this pack.

### Gaps

- No annual report, half-year report or CNMV results body text available for going-concern, covenant or contingency language.
- Cannot verify management-adjusted EBITDA, net recourse debt or dividend policy from primary sources.
- FY2025 “historic minimum debt” claim in news cannot be audited against filing extracts here.

---
risks_and_flags:
**Leverage and interest burden:** Total debt ~€9.4bn against equity ~€1.0bn; interest expense ~€708m consumes a large share of operating profit. Failed screen models on Financial Health, Buffett Quality and Economic Moat flag structural balance-sheet risk. H1 2026 news indicates net debt **rising again** as concession capex resumes — worth monitoring against the FY2025 deleveraging narrative.

**Earnings vs cash divergence:** Reported EPS fell to €0.11 in 2025 while FCF surged; minority interest deductions (€148m in 2025) and special charges complicate equity-level profitability. The screen’s 985% earnings growth input likely reflects base-effect distortion rather than sustainable trend.

**Legal / regulatory:** Panama won a major investment arbitration against Sacyr over Canal-related claims (Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas de Panamá, 31 October 2025; En Segundos Panama, same date). Shares fell on the “revés jurídico” (XTB.com, 3 November 2025). This is a material sovereign-risk and litigation overhang not captured by quantitative screens.

**Asset-sale execution:** Postponement of the Voreantis sale (XTB.com, 21 October 2025) triggered a sharp share sell-off — highlights reliance on divestments to fund the concession pivot and reduce recourse debt.

**Governance:** Family-linked control persists; AGM scheduled to re-elect Demetrio Carceller Arce (Yahoo Finanzas, 29 April 2026). Not inherently negative, but concentrated ownership warrants scrutiny of related-party and capital-allocation decisions.

**Valuation richness:** P/E 39.2 and P/B 3.8 fail most traditional value screens; the buy signal is FCF-driven. If FCF normalises lower post-divestment, the valuation case weakens quickly.

**Filing gap:** Absence of CNMV annual/interim body text means covenants, contingencies, pension obligations and going-concern assessments **cannot be reviewed** in this pass — a red flag for verify-before-trade discipline.

research_rationale: The cash-flow and concession-pivot narrative partially supports the quantitative buy signal, but extreme leverage, rich headline multiples, legal setbacks and the absence of primary filing extracts prevent full confirmation of the value case.
